claims.text: The placeholder text 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' can appear in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property when an Output is treated as if it were already a plain value.

Pulumi's docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ contains a rundown of the symptoms of treating an Output as if it were already a plain value, including the 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' message.
Resources created inside an `apply` callback will not appear in `pulumi preview` unless the output's value is already known.
Because resources created inside `apply` may not appear in `pulumi preview`, the preview output may not match the actual changes made when `pulumi up` is run.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ that diagnoses errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
Errors from stringifying an output value like a plain value are a diagnosable issue covered by Pulumi's Output Value Errors troubleshooting page.
Errors from branching on an output value like a plain value are a diagnosable issue covered by Pulumi's Output Value Errors troubleshooting page.
Errors from reading an output value like a plain value are a diagnosable issue covered by Pulumi's Output Value Errors troubleshooting page.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ that helps resolve '409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress' errors.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ that helps handle 500 internal server errors from Pulumi Cloud.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ that covers post-step event failures and engine bugs.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ that helps fix network connectivity and proxy problems.
Pulumi's using-a-diy-backend guide has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml that resolves `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when the CLI can't access a self-managed state backend.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ that helps handle scenarios when `pulumi destroy` fails.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ that helps recover from interrupted deployments.
Pulumi has a troubleshooting guide page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/ that fixes crashes or hangs on Apple Silicon caused by x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2.
Crashes or hangs on Apple Silicon Macs can be caused by x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2.
Pulumi's troubleshooting page JavaScript redirects visitors whose URL hash is '#conflict' to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
Pulumi's troubleshooting page JavaScript redirects visitors whose URL hash is '#verbose-logging' to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging.
A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports limiting operations to specific resources using the `--target` and `--exclude` flags when a stuck or misbehaving resource is blocking a wider update.
Pulumi offers pre-release ('dev') builds that provide access to bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
Pulumi has a Community Slack, accessible at https://slack.pulumi.com, that provides fast community support.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has actually been created or updated.
Pulumi's Output representation of resource properties is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

If you concatenate, log, or otherwise convert a Pulumi Output value to a string directly (in TypeScript) instead of going through `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In TypeScript, the placeholder string produced by calling toString on an Output contains literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate` instead.

In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output, or letting an Output flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value, via the same placeholder mechanism as toString.
In Python, converting an Output to a string directly (e.g. via an f-string) produces a broken string and logs a warning, without raising an exception.
In Python, the broken string produced by converting an Output to a string contains literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`.
In Python, passing a Pulumi Output to `json.dumps()` fails outright with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
Python's Pulumi SDK provides `Output.json_dumps()` as the intended replacement for calling `json.dumps()` directly on an Output.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise, due to Go's static typing.
In Go, the fix for the Output-to-string mistake is to resolve the value inside `ApplyT` and pass the result on, rather than trying to read a `pulumi.StringOutput` as a plain `string`.
In C#, converting a Pulumi Output value to a string directly (e.g. via string interpolation) silently produces a broken string without throwing an exception.

In C#, the resulting broken string from converting an Output to a string contains literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format` instead.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` in TypeScript, Python, and C# causes the Output-to-string conversion mistake to throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning placeholder text.
TypeScript provides `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` as string-composition helpers for working with Outputs.
Python provides `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` as string-composition helpers for working with Outputs.
Go provides `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` as string-composition helpers for working with Outputs.
C# provides `Output.Format` as a string-composition helper for working with Outputs.

A value read out of a Pulumi Output inside an `apply`/`Apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using that variable later outside the callback does not work as expected because the callback runs asynchronously after the outer code has already run.
The `apply` callback runs when the Pulumi engine resolves the dependency graph, not on a fixed timer, so the outer-variable-assignment mistake cannot be fixed by adding a delay.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values, so passing an Output directly as an input often removes the need for an explicit `apply` call.
A resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept a Pulumi Output value directly.

In a dynamically typed Pulumi SDK language, branching directly on an Output object (e.g. `if (someOutput) { ... }`) evaluates the output object itself rather than its eventual value, so the branch is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed Pulumi SDK language, branching directly on an Output value (e.g. treating an `Output<bool>` as a `bool`) is usually a compile error.

A plain value that is already known when a Pulumi program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, branches on it exactly as expected without the Output-branching problem.
In TypeScript, Go, and C#, passing a Pulumi Output as a resource's logical name, a loop bound, or a map key fails to compile because these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Python, passing a Pulumi Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string` at runtime.
In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a loop bound (e.g. `range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer` at runtime.

In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; instead Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, causing the lookup to silently key on the wrong thing.
Pulumi's StackReference feature allows a later, separate stack to consume outputs from a first stack when dependent resources cannot be provisioned until an earlier resource exists.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and pull a resolved value out of an Output synchronously (e.g. via `await`), and attempting to do so either fails to compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text instead of the value.
The `pulumi stack output <name>` CLI command reads a single stack output after a deployment.
A Pulumi StackReference from another Pulumi program allows one stack's outputs to be consumed as another stack's inputs.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update, accessible for example as `res.Outputs` in Go, for programmatically reading deployment outputs.
